checks.reason: The actual page defines pi0(F) as connected components of |F| with the quotient topology. The lemma assumes only locally profinite K and small v-sheaves F,G with G=F/underline K. It adds no compactness, proper action, quasiseparatedness or local spatiality. The counterexample therefore must be assessed against this generality, rather than silently against extra properties of later shtuka instances.

The root checked Definition11.1/Proposition11.3, Example11.12, Proposition11.13/Definition11.14, Example11.16 and Remark12.2. For C the completed algebraic closure of F2((t)), F=underline Z2 x Spa(C,O_C)=Spa(C0(Z2,C),C0(Z2,O_C)) is affinoid perfectoid with |F|=Z2. Discrete K=Z is locally profinite via open compact subgroup{0}. Integer translation acts on the profinite index, not the characteristic2 field; the embedding Z->Z2 is injective, so the action is free. R=coproduct_Z F has pro-etale projections, each an isomorphism on a summand, and is the representable equivalence relation. Its quotient is a diamond and small v-sheaf; the cited definition does not require the relation to be quasicompact.

checks.source_locations: Same reference quotient topology result; report analytic construction
checks.reason: The reference gives the ordinary orbit quotient topology, without a T0 or Hausdorff reflection. Any nonempty saturated open subset of Z2 contains a+2^m Z2; integer translates cover all residue classes, hence all Z2. Thus Z2/Z is indiscrete and connected. It still has at least two orbits:0 and1/3 differ by no integer. Consequently pi0(F/K) is a singleton while pi0(F)/K=Z2/Z is not; the second equality fails already as a set bijection. The first equality |F/K|=|F|/K is not refuted.

Proposition3.12 explicitly invokes Lemma3.2 for component transitivity. Proposition6.11 uses that proposition to give G(Qp)/H_t, and Lemmas6.12-6.14 use the homogeneous description in Theorem6.1(4)->(5). This is a concrete core bridge. The quotient counterexample is non-locally-spatial and its acting group noncompact; it does not refute compact Iwahori/Galois quotients or actual shtuka transitivity. Equation(3.12) in Theorem3.9 is a different specialization statement. No verified instance-specific replacement bridge has been supplied; Major does not assert the main formula is false.

Conditional on the component-induction formula, a transitive A-set A/C induces B/f(C). The forward C=N implication gives B/f(N). Conversely f(C)=f(N) alone does not imply C=N; the simply-connected action used to pass(6.8) to(6.10) needs justification in that direction. Determinant control, a finite central intersection and absence of proper finite-index subgroups offer real counterevidence in the isotropic simply-connected subcase. The general geometric stabilizer hypotheses and anisotropic case remain unresolved. No actual geometric counterexample is established, so Needs Evidence is the appropriate retained status.
